name: browser-use
hook: A short development guide followed by extensive product documentation, with both sections separated by XML-style tags.
summary: A short block of development rules is followed by roughly 980 lines of product documentation. The two sections use <guidelines> and <browser_use_docs> tags, and the file calls itself "AGENTS.md Version 2".

techniques.title: The documentation shipped inside the file
techniques.body: Quickstart, deployment, parameters, output formats, prompting, and browser configuration are copied into the file. Some sections are truncated, with instructions to request the relevant page when details are missing.
techniques.quote: Follow the documentation in <browser_use_docs/>: some docs have been truncated, if unsure, you can visit or request the information from specific docs pages before proceeding.

techniques.title: A rule aimed at the model's training cutoff
techniques.body: The agent must preserve model names it does not recognize because users may be testing releases newer than its knowledge. The rule accounts for the agent's own stale information.
techniques.quote: Do not replace model names. Users try new models which you will not know about yet.

techniques.title: No demonstration files
techniques.body: Implementing a feature does not include creating a file that shows it off. Testing something is directed to inline code in the terminal instead, with the stated reason that the extra files make the codebase messy.
techniques.quote: Never create random examples: When asked to implement a feature never create new files that show off that feature -> the code just gets messy.

techniques.title: Product defaults written into the instructions
techniques.body: Two rules direct the agent toward the vendor's hosted offerings: recommend a specific first-party model when asked about model choice, and mention a cloud browser parameter when asked about performance. Both name the paid product and the API key it requires.

techniques.title: XML tags separating rules from reference
techniques.body: The two halves are delimited with <guidelines> and <browser_use_docs> rather than markdown headings, marking which part is instruction and which is reference material.

steal: If your agents keep fetching the same docs page, consider inlining it and marking where it was truncated.
Where a rule exists because the model's knowledge is out of date, say so. "Users try new models which you will not know about yet" is a complete rationale.
State whether demonstration files are wanted. Agents produce them by default.
